_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `wavefront <repo> <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through wavefront.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: git_allocator
types._comment_agent: A plain vtable value: no lifecycle of its own. git_allocator_setup (GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR) memcpys the caller's struct into the hidden global git__allocator, so the caller's storage is borrowed for the call only. The init routines git_stdalloc_init_allocator / git_debugalloc_init_allocator fill caller storage but are not exported from libgit2.so (declared without GIT_EXTERN, hidden), and git_win32_crtdbg_init_allocator is declared but never defined on this build; the only public producer is a value the caller fills itself. The three members form one allocator family: storage from gmalloc/grealloc must be released by the same family's grealloc/gfree, and libgit2 calls them from any thread.

ptr.note: Function pointer to code: static. Releases a live allocation of this allocator; NULL is a no-op. Called unconditionally by git__free, so it must be set when installed.

Function pointer to code: static, never owned or freed. libgit2 calls it unconditionally through git__allocator (git__malloc, threadstate_get), so every installed allocator must set it (git2/sys/alloc.h: 'all fields need to be set'); the C type admits NULL (bindgen Option), which only a never-installed value may hold. Returns fresh storage of >= n bytes or NULL; file/line are the call site (__FILE__, a static string) and are borrowed for the call.

Function pointer to code: static. C realloc contract: consumes a live allocation of this allocator (or NULL = malloc) and returns a new one of `size` bytes, or NULL leaving the old one live. Called unconditionally by git__realloc / git__reallocarray, so it must be set when installed.

types.name: git_branch_t
types._comment_agent: core wave 0 batch 0 (2026-10-09). Flag-shaped enum: LOCAL = 1, REMOTE = 2, ALL = LOCAL|REMOTE. git_branch_iterator_new stores it as unsigned flags and git_branch_next tests each bit (0 lists nothing, extra bits are ignored) and writes only LOCAL or REMOTE to *out_type; git_branch_lookup switches on it and hits GIT_ASSERT(false) for any other value (-1 'unrecoverable internal error' in release, abort in the Debug/coverage build). Wrapped as the closed Rust enum BranchType, so the asserting values are unrepresentable.

types.name: git_buf
types._comment_agent: core wave 0 batch 0 (2026-10-09). Wrapped as Buf / BufRef / BufMut, owned by value as BufVal = CVal<Buf, BufDispose>; the safe API keeps the invariant 'reserved == 0 owns nothing and reads empty; reserved > 0 owns a libgit2-allocator buffer with size < reserved and ptr[size] == NUL'. BufDispose calls git_buf_dispose only when reserved > 0. Review (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09): Buf::from_raw's contract now also requires ptr[0..size) initialised and exclusive while the owner lives; git_repository_discover is the one public filler that skips git_buf_tostr.

ptr.note: A byte buffer of `size` bytes, NUL-terminated at ptr[size] (contents may hold interior NULs: diff/patch/pack output). Ownership is runtime-conditional: libgit2's producers (git_buf_fromstr) leave reserved = git_str asize, so reserved > 0 means ptr is a git__malloc buffer of >= reserved bytes the struct owns, writable and reusable (git_buf_sanitize writes ptr[0], git_buf_tostr adopts it as git_str asize and may git__realloc it). reserved == 0 means it owns nothing: ptr is NULL (GIT_BUF_INIT) or the hidden static git_str__initstr (size 0), which git_buf_tostr/sanitize replace without freeing. git_buf_dispose itself frees any ptr != git_str__initstr (git__free(NULL) for GIT_BUF_INIT, which reads git__allocator unsynchronised against a first git_libgit2_init), so a reserved == 0 buffer with a foreign non-NULL ptr would be freed by dispose yet dropped by sanitize. The one producer of that shape is the internal git_merge_driver__builtin_apply (merged_out reserved = 0 over an owned, non-NUL-terminated merge result, disposed by merge_conflict_invoke_driver); no public routine hands it out. The header's 'reserved and unused' comment is wrong. Every public producer first passes the caller's struct through git_buf_tostr (reusing or git__realloc-ing a reserved > 0 allocation, or dropping a reserved == 0 ptr) except git_repository_discover, which writes `out` with git_buf_fromstr(out, &paths.gitdir) directly: a reserved > 0 allocation handed in is overwritten and LEAKED (no use-after-free: fromstr moves the git_str out before repo_paths_dispose). Its wrapper must fill a fresh Buf::new(), as the convention already says (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09).

types.name: git_buildinfo_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless enum, passed by value only; no pointer, no lifecycle (core wave 0 batch 1, 2026-10-09). Sole consumer git_libgit2_buildinfo (settings.c:478) switches on it: GIT_BUILDINFO_CPU (1) returns the static string GIT_BUILD_CPU, GIT_BUILDINFO_COMMIT (2) the static GIT_BUILD_COMMIT, each only when cmake defined it (CPU always, COMMIT when `git rev-parse HEAD` succeeded at configure time); every other value, 0 included, returns NULL without setting an error. The returned strings are static, never freed. Rust: `BuildInfo` (#[repr(u32)], fallible from_raw) in core/common.rs.

types.name: git_error
types._comment_agent: Published only as `const git_error *` by git_error_last, which never returns NULL: a static error, or &error_threadstate.error of the calling thread, whose fields libgit2 overwrites on the next git_error_set*/git_error_clear on that thread, so a borrow is only valid until the next libgit2 call there and must not cross threads. klass is a git_error_t value stored as int. Its lifecycle routines (git_error_save = alloc constructor through out, git_error_free / git_error_restore = droppers, statics skipped by IS_STATIC_ERROR) are internal to libgit2.so (src/util/errors.h, hidden), so a wrapper copies a published error into Rust storage instead.

ptr.note: Runtime-conditional ownership. In every git_error libgit2 publishes (git_error_last) it is borrowed: for the per-thread error it aliases error_threadstate.message.ptr (a git_str the thread state owns; set_error_from_buffer), so it dangles once the next error on that thread grows the buffer (git_str_puts/vprintf realloc) and dies with the thread state (thread exit, git_libgit2_shutdown); for the four static errors (oom, uninitialized, tlsdata, no_error) it is a static string literal. Only in the private copies made by git_error_save is it owned: a git__strdup that git_error_free / git_error_restore release with git__free. Never NULL in a published error (the thread state's git_str is initialised to git_str__initstr and set_error_from_buffer is skipped on OOM); C callers (fetchhead_ref_parse, local_push, git_fs_path_direach) read it unchecked. Never written through: libgit2 writes the git_str and re-points the field.

types.name: git_error_code
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum (bindgen: c_int constants, values 0 and -1..-40 with gaps at -2 and -25..-29). No storage, no pointer, no lifecycle: libgit2 never names the type in a signature, every API returns or accepts these codes as plain int, and callbacks may return any int (positive values and unknown negatives are passed through, e.g. git_error_set_after_callback), so a raw int is not guaranteed to be a variant. GIT_EUSER is never produced by libgit2; GIT_RETRY is internal. Wrapped as a Rust enum whose discriminants are the bindgen constants, converted from int fallibly (from_raw -> Option) and never transmuted.

types.name: git_error_t
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum of error classes (bindgen: c_uint constants 0..=36, contiguous). No storage, no pointer, no lifecycle. Consumers carry it as int: git_error.klass (int, @type git_error_t) and git_error_set/git_error_set_str(int error_class, ...), which accept any int from user code, so git_error_last()->klass may hold a value outside the enum. Wrapped as a Rust enum with discriminants from the bindgen constants, converted from int fallibly (from_raw -> Option).

types.name: git_feature_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless bit-flag enum (1<<0 .. 1<<12), by value only; no pointer, no lifecycle (core wave 0 batch 1, 2026-10-09). Two consumers with different cardinality: git_libgit2_features (libgit2.c:83) returns an `int` OR-ing the compiled-in features (scalar set; HTTP_PARSER, REGEX, COMPRESSION, SHA1, SHA256 always), and git_libgit2_feature_backend (libgit2.c:118) takes ONE value and switches on it, returning a static backend string or NULL (unnamed values, combinations, HTTP always, and features compiled out). Its GIT_ASSERT_WITH_RETVAL branches (feature compiled in with an unknown backend) are unreachable in configured builds but would set an error (pre-init TLS hazard) or abort in Debug. Rust: `Feature` (#[repr(u32)] single value) and `Features` (c_int set, unnamed bits retained) in core/common.rs.

types.name: git_filemode_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum of octal UNIX modes (UNREADABLE 0, TREE 0040000, BLOB 0100644, BLOB_EXECUTABLE 0100755, LINK 0120000, COMMIT 0160000; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Unnamed values flow through it: git_tree_entry_filemode_raw (tree.c:255) returns git_tree_entry.attr (uint16_t) as parsed by parse_mode (tree.c:371, any octal value 0..=0177777, larger -> git_tree_lookup -1 GIT_ERROR_TREE 'failed to parse tree: can't parse filemode'), e.g. old git's 0100664 or 0, which reads as UNREADABLE; git_tree_entry_filemode normalises (normalize_filemode, tree.c:35: type 04 -> TREE, any 0100 exec bit -> BLOB_EXECUTABLE before the 016/012 checks, so 0160755 -> BLOB_EXECUTABLE, else BLOB), always one of the five insertable values. git_treebuilder_insert (and git_tree_create_updated through it) accepts exactly TREE/BLOB/BLOB_EXECUTABLE/LINK/COMMIT (valid_filemode tree.c:26), refusing everything else, UNREADABLE included, with -1 GIT_ERROR_TREE 'failed to insert entry: invalid filemode for file - <name>' before touching the builder; with strict object creation on, TREE must name a tree and BLOB/EXEC/LINK a blob, COMMIT is unchecked. UNREADABLE marks an unreadable workdir file in iterator.c:1444. git_diff_file.mode (uint16_t) and git_index_entry.mode (uint32_t) carry these values untyped. Rust side (core/types.rs FileMode): never transmute; convert fallibly (FileMode::from_raw / TryFrom -> UnnamedFileMode); a tree-entry wrapper should return Result<FileMode, UnnamedFileMode> (or the raw u32) for filemode_raw and may expect a named value from filemode; a treebuilder insert wrapper taking FileMode must still expect UNREADABLE to be refused.

types.name: git_libgit2_opt_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum of the keys git_libgit2_opts (settings.c:105) dispatches on, dense 0..=47 (GIT_OPT_GET_MWINDOW_SIZE .. GIT_OPT_SET_PACK_MAX_OBJECT_SIZE; bindgen types it c_uint, but git_libgit2_opts takes `int option, ...`). No storage or lifecycle. Every value without a constant (negative included) hits the default arm: -1, GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid option key', and no va_arg is read, so calling with the bare key is sound. Each named key fixes the variadic argument list (documented per variant in core/common.rs LibraryOption). Hazards for the git_libgit2_opts wrapper: SET_SSL_CIPHERS strdups its argument with no NULL check (NULL = crash); SET_ALLOCATOR memcpys a git_allocator (NULL restores stdalloc) and swaps the global allocator under live allocations; GET/SET_WINDOWS_SHAREMODE are no-ops off Windows (the out pointer is left unwritten, rc 0); SET_SSL_CERT_LOCATIONS with OpenSSL fails GIT_ERROR_SSL when neither location loads; ADD_SSL_X509_CERT(NULL) adds nothing and returns 0; SET_SEARCH_PATH/GET_SEARCH_PATH take an int config level, only SYSTEM(2)/XDG(3)/GLOBAL(4) accepted (GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid config path selector %d'); SET_SERVER_(CONNECT_)TIMEOUT refuse negatives (GIT_ERROR_INVALID); SET_OWNER_VALIDATION stores !=0; GET_EXTENSIONS hands out a git_strarray to dispose; GET_* buf options fill a git_buf. Settings are unsynchronised globals (git_sysdir_set etc.). Rust side: LibraryOption::from_raw/from_key/TryFrom -> UnnamedLibraryOption; key() gives the int.

types.name: git_object_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_OBJECT_ANY = -2, GIT_OBJECT_INVALID = -1, COMMIT 1, TREE 2, BLOB 3, TAG 4; bindgen types it c_int). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value, and through out-params (git_odb_read_header, git_odb_read_prefix-style backend callbacks in sys/odb_backend.h, git_odb_expand_id.type in/out). Only 1..=4 name an object's type: git_object_type_is_valid (object.c:344) accepts exactly those (git_objects_table size > 0); type2string gives '' for any other value; string2type returns INVALID for unknown, NULL or empty names (it prefix-matches, so 'commitx' -> COMMIT). GIT_OBJECT_ANY is a lookup/peel filter only (object_lookup*, git_object_peel, git_reference_peel, tree_entry_to_object, odb expand_ids), never an object's type; INVALID is an error/unset answer (git_object_type(NULL), git_tag_target_type(NULL), git_tree_entry_type(NULL), string2type misses, parse placeholders). The pack-entry types 6/7 are the GIT_PACKFILE_OFS_DELTA/REF_DELTA macros (pack.h:37), packfile-only, never a public out-param; cache.c's per-type limit table still reserves slots 0 and 5..7, so GIT_OPT_SET_CACHE_OBJECT_LIMIT accepts any of 0..=7 and rejects others 'type out of range' (cache.c:36). git_odb_expand_ids reads 0 as ANY and writes 0 back on a miss. HAZARD (probed, plain build): git_odb_write(..., type 0) succeeds - normalize_options (object.c:630) reads object_type 0 as BLOB for the id, but the loose backend formats its header from type2string(0) = '', so it stores an object under a blob id that git_odb_read_header then fails on ('failed to read loose object header'), and a later real write of the same blob is skipped by git_odb__freshen. Every other unnamed value (<0, >=5) is rejected 'invalid object type'. Rust side (core/types.rs): ObjectType {Commit, Tree, Blob, Tag}, #[repr(i32)], non_exhaustive; never transmute: from_raw/TryFrom<git_object_t> -> NotAnObjectType for every other value; filters spell ANY as None through ObjectType::raw_or_any(Option<ObjectType>), so a typed write/hash wrapper cannot pass 0.

types.name: git_oid
types._comment_agent: Plain value type with no pointer fields: `type` (unsigned char holding a git_oid_t value, 0 = GIT_OID_NONE/unset) and `id` (32-byte inline array, GIT_OID_MAX_SIZE). Never heap-allocated by libgit2's public API on its own; callers hold it by value or receive `const git_oid *` into a parent object. Nothing to release. Every bit pattern is accepted by oid.c: an unknown `type` makes git_oid_size/hexsize return 0 and the formatters report 'unknown type' (git_oid_nfmt/pathfmt) - BUT git_oid_tostr_s then returns its per-thread buffer without writing it (uninitialised on the thread's first call, no NUL: ASan heap-buffer-overflow in strlen confirmed with a zeroed oid), so its wrapper must reject unknown types. All-zero is libgit2's own GIT_OID_NONE. Constructors (init into caller storage): git_oid_from_string, git_oid_from_prefix, git_oid_from_raw; cloner: git_oid_cpy (memcpy of the whole struct; overlapping out/src would be UB).

types.name: git_oid_shorten
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/oid.h, defined in oid.c); only oid.c touches its fields. Constructor git_oid_shorten_new (git__calloc + 16-node trie; NULL on OOM or when min_length does not fit an int - a hard assert(3) in _DEBUG builds), dropper git_oid_shorten_free (NULL-safe). No cloner. git_oid_shorten_add keeps borrowed pointers into its text_oid argument and validates only the characters it walks, so a short or non-hex id stored as a tail later yields git__fromhex == -1 and push_leaf writes children[-1], silently corrupting the preceding trie node (in bounds of the buffer, so ASan does not flag it; probe: add("azzz") then add("ab0...0") both succeed): its wrapper must accept only full 40-char hex ids, borrowed for the shortener's lifetime.

ptr.note: Trie buffer of `size` trie_node unions, allocated by resize_trie through git__reallocarray and released by git_oid_shorten_free (git__free). Each node is either 16 child indices or a leaf whose `tail` is a BORROWED `const char *` into a text id the caller passed to git_oid_shorten_add (retained after the call: the shortener reads the tail again when a later id shares the prefix), so the shortener must not outlive any string added to it. NULL after a failed resize inside git_oid_shorten_add: resize_trie assigns the realloc result before checking it, leaking the old buffer and leaving nodes == NULL with size unchanged, so the next add dereferences NULL; only git_oid_shorten_free remains safe on such an object.

types.name: git_oid_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_OID_SHA1 = 1, GIT_OID_SHA256 = 2, both unconditional in include/git2/oid.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Unnamed values flow through it: 0 means 'unset' in every *_options.oid_type - read as GIT_OID_DEFAULT (SHA1) by repository.c:356/364 (git_repository_new, which GIT_ASSERT_ARGs validity of a non-zero value), odb.c:307, index.c:447, commit_graph.c:431 and midx.c:537 (both assert validity after defaulting), indexer.c:178, object.c:633, diff_parse.c:91, but as the repository's own type by git_diff_options (diff_generate.c:502: 0 -> repo->oid_type, a non-zero mismatch is GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'specified object ID type does not match repository object ID type'). Public routines also hand 0 out: git_repository_oid_type(NULL) returns 0 (repository.c:4076) and git_remote_oid_type writes *out = 0 before failing (remote.c:1040); git_oid_type_fromstr/fromstrn return 0 for an unknown name (load_objectformat -> GIT_EINVALID 'unknown object format'). git_repository_init_ext validates opts->oid_type not at all (repository.c:2936): an unnamed value is written to extensions.objectformat as git_oid_type_name's 'unknown' and the just-created repository fails to open (GIT_EINVALID, directory left behind). git_oid_size/hexsize/type_is_valid reject anything but 1 and 2 (src/libgit2/oid.h:27-54), so git_oid_from_* return -1 'unknown type'. git_oid.type stores it narrowed to unsigned char. Rust side: never transmute; convert fallibly (OidType::from_raw / TryFrom<git_oid_t>); option-field accessors should map 0 to None and typed setters make the init_ext quirk unreachable; returned values go through from_raw too.

types.name: git_oidarray
types._comment_agent: By-value C struct {ids, count}, never allocated by libgit2 itself (header: 'the library will never allocate that object directly'): callers own it inline and dispose its ids with git_oidarray_dispose. All-zero is the empty array and dispose accepts it (git__free(NULL)); before git_libgit2_init git__free is failalloc's no-op, but git__free reads git__allocator.gfree unsynchronised, and the first git_libgit2_init (git_allocator_global_init -> git_stdalloc_init_allocator) or GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR writes it: disposing an empty array on one thread while another thread initialises the library is a data race (TSan, oid review wave 1 batch 0). Only the empty array can reach that, since nothing allocated for it; the Rust OidArrayDispose therefore skips the C call when ids is NULL. count must not exceed the buffer's length; ids must be non-NULL when count > 0 (git_repository__shallow_roots_write indexes it unconditionally). Not address-sensitive. No refcount, no lock. Deprecated alias git_oidarray_free is compiled hidden under DEPRECATE_HARD. Wrapped as OidArray / OidArrayVal = CVal<OidArray, OidArrayDispose> with ids moved in/out as OdbDataVec<Oid> (git_odb_backend_data_alloc/free = git__malloc/git__free).

ptr.note: A buffer of `count` git_oid values in libgit2's allocator (git__allocator), owned by the struct and released by git_oidarray_dispose -> git__free (which does not reset the fields). Producers: git_merge_bases / git_merge_bases_many hand over a git_array_oid_t's ptr (git_oidarray__from_array; grown by git__reallocarray, so asize may exceed count), git_smart__shallow_roots git__malloc's a copy (NULL for 0). NULL whenever count == 0 on every libgit2 path (git_array_init leaves ptr NULL until the first alloc; smart sets NULL); fetch.c/compute_base start from {0}. Elements are written in place (git_oidarray__reverse), read by index (git_repository__shallow_roots_write, oidarray_contains, compute_base). A transport's shallow_roots callback (git2/sys/transport.h) fills `out` with an allocation libgit2 later frees with git_oidarray_dispose, so a user-filled array must be git__malloc storage (git_odb_backend_data_alloc is the exported route). git_oidarray__to_array lends the buffer to a git_array without transferring ownership.

types.name: git_reference_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_REFERENCE_INVALID = 0, DIRECT = 1, SYMBOLIC = 2, ALL = DIRECT|SYMBOLIC = 3; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle. Its only public flow is the return of git_reference_type (refs.c:339), which answers ref->type: DIRECT or SYMBOLIC for every git_reference libgit2 builds (git_reference__alloc / __alloc_symbolic, refs.c:60/85); with NULL it GIT_ASSERT_ARGs, returning -1 (u32::MAX through the unsigned enum) in a release build and aborting in the Debug/coverage build. INVALID is internal only (transaction.c node with no target set); ALL is a list-filter mask that no non-deprecated API takes (only deprecated GIT_REF_LISTALL). No public routine takes a git_reference_t argument. Rust side (core/types.rs): ReferenceType {Direct, Symbolic}, #[repr(u32)], non_exhaustive; from_raw/TryFrom<git_reference_t> -> NotAReferenceType for INVALID, ALL and every unnamed value; never transmute.

types.name: git_signature
types._comment_agent: git_signature is a heap object owned by a single holder: CBox<Signature, SignatureFree> (git_signature_free drops it with both strings; git_signature_dup deep-copies it, refusing NULL fields that C would strdup). Public consumers otherwise receive `const git_signature *` borrowed from a parent (git_commit_author/committer, git_tag_tagger, git_note_author/committer, git_reflog_entry_committer, git_blame_hunk fields) and only read it; every `const git_signature *` argument (commit/tag/note/reflog/stash/rebase creation) is only read and copied, so a caller-built struct over borrowed strings (SignatureView) is a valid argument. `when` is an embedded git_time value. No refcount, no lock. Constructors: git_signature_new, git_signature_now, git_signature_from_buffer (alloc through out-param), git_signature_default / git_signature_default_from_env (need a git_repository; left to the object/signature symbol batch). C defects: git_signature_new leaks p (and p->name) when a string allocation fails; git_signature_dup leaks the partial copy on OOM; git_signature_default_from_env frees author/committer with git__free on error, leaking their strings.

ptr.note: NUL-terminated author email; same ownership as `name`: allocated by git_signature_new / from_buffer / dup from libgit2's allocator and freed by git_signature_free with git__free; pool-borrowed only in git_transaction's internal git_signature__pdup copies. NULL after an allocation failure inside git_signature__parse (unchecked extract_trimmed), which git_signature_dup and the commit writer then dereference. Never written through.

NUL-terminated author name. Owned on every public path: git_signature_new / git_signature_from_buffer (git__substrdup via extract_trimmed) and git_signature_dup (git__strdup) allocate it from libgit2's allocator, and git_signature_free releases it with git__free (also called by git_commit__free, git_tag__free, git_reflog_entry__free, git_note_free, free_hunk on the signatures those objects own). Borrowed only in the internal git_signature__pdup copies a git_transaction keeps in its pool (transaction.c copy_common / dup_reflog), which are never freed individually and never reach a public consumer. Nullable: git_signature__parse does not check extract_trimmed's result, so an allocation failure leaves it NULL while the parse (git_signature_from_buffer, commit/tag/reflog parsing) still succeeds; refdb_reftable_log_fill checks for that, git_signature_dup (strdup(NULL)) and git_signature__writebuf (%s) do not. A calloc'd signature is NULL before parse. Never written through; libgit2 only reads, copies or frees it. Rust: Option<&CStr> getter on SignatureRef, replacement setters taking an OdbDataStr (git__malloc storage released by git__free) on SignatureMut.

types.name: git_strarray
types._comment_agent: Wrapped in core/strarray.rs (core wave 0 batch 4) as StrArray + StrArrayVal = CVal<StrArray, StrArrayDispose> for the owned form (strings move as OdbDataStrVec), and StrArrayView<'a> for the borrowed input form, which hands out StrArrayRef only. git_strarray_copy (the deep cloner) is hidden under DEPRECATE_HARD, so copies go through OdbDataStrVec::dup_all. git_strarray_dispose is skipped for a NULL `strings` (empty state; see the first-init allocator race).

ptr.note: A buffer of `count` NUL-terminated `char *` elements. Two statically distinct contracts, decided by API direction. (1) OUTPUT (git_reference_list, git_tag_list(_match), git_remote_list, git_worktree_list, git_remote_get_fetch/push_refspecs via copy_refspecs, git_remote_rename problems, GIT_OPT_GET_EXTENSIONS, store_refs): libgit2 writes `strings`/`count` without disposing what the struct held, from a git_vector (git_vector_detach / .contents, i.e. git__reallocarray storage with spare capacity) whose elements are git__strdup'd; the struct owns the array and every string, and git_strarray_dispose frees strings[0..count) then the array with git__free, then zeroes the struct. git_vector_init(&v, 8) allocates eagerly, so an empty result is often a NON-NULL array with count 0 (refs.c, tag.c, remote.c, repository.c extensions); worktree.c and the error paths leave NULL/0. Producers never store a NULL element. (2) INPUT (`const git_strarray *` args: git_index_add_all/remove_all/update_all, git_remote_fetch/push/upload/download/connect, git_reset_default, git_pathspec_new, git_stash_save_with_opts, and by-value option fields: git_diff_options.pathspec, git_checkout_options.paths, custom_headers, remote_push_options): libgit2 only reads strings[0..count) (pathspec/iterator/headers deref every element, so NULL elements are invalid), copies what it keeps (git_strarray_copy, git__strdup), and never frees or writes the caller's array: borrowed for the call / the options' lifetime. git_remote_connect memcpys the caller's struct into its options and copies it via git_remote_connect_options_dup before use. NULL `strings` means empty only with count 0; git_strarray_dispose with NULL strings and count > 0 derefs NULL. Owned arrays are written (dispose zeroes, producers fill), borrowed ones are const.

types.name: git_submodule_ignore_t
types._comment_agent: Values -1 (UNSPECIFIED), 1 NONE, 2 UNTRACKED, 3 DIRTY, 4 ALL; 0 is unnamed (the old GIT_SUBMODULE_IGNORE_DEFAULT the types.h comment still mentions is gone). Consumers: git_submodule_status / git_submodule__status read UNSPECIFIED as 'the submodule's configured value' and compare the rest for equality (any other value behaves like UNTRACKED). git_diff_options.ignore_submodules: `<= 0` (0 from a zeroed struct, or UNSPECIFIED from GIT_DIFF_OPTIONS_INIT) means 'read diff.ignoreSubmodules' (diff_generate.c:561). git_submodule_set_ignore maps through _sm_ignore_map, so UNSPECIFIED, 0 and anything outside 1..4 fail with GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for ignore'. Producers (git_submodule_ignore, git_submodule_parse_ignore from config strings none/untracked/dirty/all/true/false) only return 1..4, plus UNSPECIFIED from git_submodule_ignore(NULL) via GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL. Wrapped as core::types::SubmoduleIgnore (repr(i32)), converted fallibly with from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_recurse_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_RECURSE_NO = 0, _YES = 1, _ONDEMAND = 2, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Producers: submodule_parse_recurse (submodule.c:2034) maps .gitmodules/config fetchRecurseSubmodules through _sm_recurse_map (bool false->NO, true->YES, 'on-demand' case-insensitive->ONDEMAND); an unreadable spelling writes YES to *out then fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'recurse' property: '<v>''; an unset setting leaves the alloc default NO (submodule.c:1962). git_submodule_fetch_recurse_submodules returns sm->fetch_recurse unchanged (only named values; NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NO in release, abort in the Debug/coverage build). Consumer: git_submodule_set_fetch_recurse_submodules -> write_mapped_var -> git_config_lookup_map_enum: unnamed values fail -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for fetchRecurseSubmodules'; YES writes 'true', ONDEMAND 'on-demand', NO (CONFIGMAP_FALSE, str NULL) DELETES the .gitmodules key and so fails GIT_ENOTFOUND (GIT_ERROR_CONFIG 'could not find key 'submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules' to delete') when the key is absent, although the submodule already reads NO. Rust: SubmoduleRecurse in core/types.rs, converted fallibly (from_raw/TryFrom -> UnnamedSubmoduleRecurse), Default = No (unset). The submodule symbol batch should treat that ENOTFOUND as success or pre-check, and route returned values through from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_update_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_CHECKOUT = 1, _REBASE = 2, _MERGE = 3, _NONE = 4, _DEFAULT = 0, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. DEFAULT (0) is never produced and never accepted: git_submodule_parse_update (submodule.c:2020) maps only via _sm_update_map ('checkout','rebase','merge','none' case-insensitive, bool true->CHECKOUT, false->NONE; an unreadable spelling writes CHECKOUT to *out and fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'update' property: '<v>''), an unset setting keeps the alloc default CHECKOUT (submodule.c:1961), git_submodule_update_strategy maps any value < CHECKOUT to CHECKOUT (NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NONE in release, abort in Debug), and git_submodule_set_update -> write_mapped_var refuses 0 and every other unnamed value with -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for update'; named values are written to .gitmodules by name ('checkout','rebase','merge','none'). git_submodule_init writes submodule.<name>.update into .git/config via submodule_update_to_str for every value but CHECKOUT (whose entry it removes); its NULL return is unreachable. The header's GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_RESET does not exist. Rust: SubmoduleUpdate in core/types.rs has no variant for DEFAULT (from_raw(0) = None, UnnamedSubmoduleUpdate), Default = Checkout so from_raw(raw).unwrap_or_default() resolves 0 as C does; typed setters can then never send a value C refuses.

types.name: git_time
types._comment_agent: Plain resource-free value (int64 seconds, int offset in minutes, char sign); no pointer field, no lifecycle routine: held by value (embedded in git_signature.when, copied field-wise by git_signature_dup/__pdup) and never released. git_signature_new sets sign = offset < 0 ? '-' : '+'. git_signature__parse leaves a calloc'd 0 sign/offset without a timezone, stores tz_start[0] verbatim as sign (any byte, not only '+'/'-') with offset 0 for a malformed timezone, and keeps the zeroes when hours > 14 or mins > 59. git_signature__writebuf (the one writer: commit, tag and reflog creation) prints '-' when offset < 0 or sign == '-' (the '-0000' case), '+' otherwise, hours/minutes from |offset| with %02d%02d, and the SECONDS THROUGH `(unsigned)sig->when.time` (%u): a time before the epoch or past 2106 is written wrapped modulo 2^32; it negates a negative offset as an int, so offset == INT_MIN overflows (C UB; the UBSan build aborts) - wrappers of the writing routines must refuse or document such a Time (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09; tests/equiv/types.rs::signature_zones_are_written_from_offset_and_sign). git_signature__equal compares the three fields. All-zero is a valid value. Wrapped as Time/TimeRef/TimeMut in core/types.rs (CZeroable, Copy, Send/Sync).

types.name: git_trace_level_t
types._comment_agent: C enum, values 0..6 (NONE..TRACE), passed by value. Consumers: git_trace_set stores any value in git_trace__data.level (GIT_ASSERT_ARG level == 0 || callback != NULL, an abort in Debug builds); git_trace() emits when git_trace__data.level >= level, so the integer order is the verbosity order; internal emitters only pass named levels (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE) to git_trace_cb. Wrapped as the fieldless TraceLevel enum (repr u32, Ord over the C values) with a fallible from_raw in core/trace.rs.

types.name: git_writestream
types._comment_agent: git_writestream is a vtable header embedded as the first member of a concrete stream (blob_writestream, buffered_stream, buf_stream, checkout_stream, user filter streams); its three members take the header pointer and cast it back to the container, so a header is never valid detached from its container (never copied or held by value). Ownership: git_blob_create_from_stream returns an owned stream (released by its own `free`, or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit); git_filter_list_stream_{buffer,file,blob} borrow a caller target for the call and write/close (never free) it; a user filter's git_filter_stream_fn returns an owned stream to libgit2, which frees it with its `free` member after closing the chain, and gets `next` borrowed for the chain's life. Rust wrapper: WriteStream/WriteStreamRef/WriteStreamMut (core/types.rs), WriteStreamBox = CBox<WriteStream, WriteStreamFree> (free through the object's own member), RustWriteStream<W: StreamWriter> for Rust implementations.

ptr.note: Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL. Finishes the stream; afterwards only `free` is valid (buf_stream/checkout_stream GIT_ASSERT on a second close, buffered_stream reruns its filter and closes its target again, blob close zeroes the filebuf so commit/write call a NULL fn). git_filter_list_stream_* call it exactly once on the head of the chain, and each buffered stream closes its target once; the user-supplied target is closed but never freed by libgit2. git_blob_create_from_stream documents that its stream must not be closed by the caller (commit flushes the filebuf close discarded).

Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL: the stream's own destructor, releasing the CONTAINING object (blob_writestream_free: filebuf cleanup + git__free(hintpath) + git__free(stream); buffered_stream_free: disposes its bufs + git__free; buf_stream_free / checkout_stream_free: no-op for stack streams). It is the type's dropper, recoverable from the object, so the Rust release strategy (WriteStreamFree) is stateless. Valid after close or without close. libgit2 frees the streams it creates (filter_streams_free) and a user filter's stream returned through git_filter_stream_fn, never the caller's target; git_blob_create_from_stream_commit frees its argument.

Function pointer (code, static lifetime), set once by every producer at construction (blob_writestream_write, buffered_stream_write, buf_stream_write, checkout_stream_write) and never rewritten; never NULL. Called as stream->write(stream, buf, len) with `stream` = the header itself, which each implementation casts back to its container struct (git_writestream is the first member `parent`/`base`), so the member is only valid for the object it was read from. `< 0` is failure (callers test `< 0`; buffered_stream_close tests `== 0`). Calling it after `close` is invalid: blob streams then call a NULL filebuf write fn (git_filebuf_cleanup zeroes the filebuf), checkout streams write to a closed (possibly reused) fd, buf_stream fails GIT_ASSERT (abort in Debug builds).

The blob_writestream header (cast back to its container), released with its filebuf and hintpath; installed as git_writestream.free by git_blob_create_from_stream, and called by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit and on its own error path.

The buffered_stream header (cast back to its container); disposes input/temp_buf and git__frees the container, leaving the target alone. Installed as git_writestream.free; called by filter_streams_free.
libc calloc: ZEROING; NULL on overflow or failure. Released by free.
libc free: releases malloc/calloc/realloc storage; NULL is a no-op.
git__malloc(nelem*elsize) then memset 0: ZEROING; NULL on multiplication overflow (no error set) or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.

git__allocator.gfree(ptr): releases any git__malloc-family storage without reading it; NULL is a no-op (stdalloc free, failalloc no-op). Internal; publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_free.

git__allocator.gmalloc(len): NON-zeroing; NULL on OOM with git_error_set_oom; always NULL before git_libgit2_init (failalloc). Internal (hidden visibility); publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_alloc. Released by git__free.
git__reallocarray(NULL, nelem, elsize): NON-zeroing array storage; NULL on overflow or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.
Read for strlen(str)+1 bytes during the call only; NULL is dereferenced (crash), so not nullable.

Fresh git__malloc(strlen(str)+1) storage holding a copy of str with its terminator: the NUL-terminated string cloner behind git_strarray_copy, git_signature_new/dup and most libgit2 string fields. NULL on OOM (git_error_set_oom via git__malloc; before git_libgit2_init every request fails). Internal (hidden visibility): Rust reproduces it as OdbDataStrFree::dup / str_dup over git_odb_backend_data_alloc; released by git__free, publicly git_odb_backend_data_free.
Read for p_strnlen(str, n) bytes during the call only: a NUL within the first n bytes ends the copy, so the input may be an unterminated run of n bytes.

Fresh git__malloc(len+1) storage holding the first len = strnlen(str, n) bytes of str plus a terminator: a bounded string cloner. NULL on OOM. Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Read for exactly n bytes during the call only, NUL or not: the caller bounds the run (a path component, a token).

Fresh git__malloc(n+1) storage holding the n bytes at str plus a terminator: a byte-run-to-string cloner. NULL on OOM or when n+1 overflows to 0 only through malloc(0) semantics (no overflow check). Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Optional filter hint path; git__strdup'd into the stream, so borrowed for the call only.

Out-slot (GIT_ASSERT_ARG): on success receives a fresh git__calloc'd blob_writestream header, owned by the caller and released by its own `free` member or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit; untouched on failure.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; stored unretained in the stream (stream->repo), which commit later uses: the repository must outlive the stream.

Must be a stream from git_blob_create_from_stream (cast to blob_writestream unchecked) that was never closed (close zeroes the filebuf; the flush then calls a NULL write fn). Consumed on every path: blob_writestream_free runs on success and failure.
Out-parameter: the new blob's id, written on success only (git_blob__create_from_paths).

The caller's git_buf, held by value (stack or embedded); NULL is a no-op. Frees buf->ptr with git__free unless it is the static git_str__initstr (NULL included), then resets the struct to {git_str__initstr, 0, 0}: reusable, never freed itself.
Releases a git_error_save copy (message, then the struct, with git__free); NULL and the static errors are ignored. Internal (hidden).

Never NULL. Points at one of four static errors (uninitialized_error before git_libgit2_init / after the last shutdown, tlsdata_error when the thread state cannot be allocated, no_error, oom_error) or at the calling thread's error_threadstate.error, whose message aliases the thread's git_str buffer; the next git_error_set*/git_error_clear on that thread (any failing libgit2 call) rewrites it and may reallocate the message, and thread exit or the last git_libgit2_shutdown frees it. Borrow valid only until the next libgit2 call on the thread: copy out (ErrorBuf). Caller must not free.

Consumes a git_error_save result: makes it the thread's last error (a static one by pointer, a copy by re-setting its class and message) and then releases it with git_error_free. NULL is rejected (GIT_ASSERT_ARG). Internal (hidden).

Out slot. Receives either a fresh git__malloc copy of the thread's last error (message git__strdup'ed), owned by the caller and released by git_error_free / git_error_restore, or one of the static errors (no_error, oom_error, tlsdata_error, or the static last error itself), which those routines skip (IS_STATIC_ERROR). Leaks the copy when the message strdup fails. Internal (src/util/errors.h, hidden).

printf-style format read during the call only (git_str_vprintf into the thread's error buffer), together with the variadic arguments it names; never retained. NULL is accepted: the message is then empty, or for GIT_ERROR_OS just strerror(errno). With GIT_ERROR_OS and a non-NULL fmt, ': ' and strerror(errno) are appended when errno != 0, and errno is reset to 0. Allocation failure leaves `last` at the static oom_error (git__realloc -> git_error_set_oom) and the thread's buffer stuck at git_str__oom, so later messages on that thread are dropped. Like every errors.c entry point, it reads TLS under errors.c's tls_key, which only exists while the runtime is initialised (pre-init it reads key 0's foreign block). Safe Rust passes "%s" with a &CStr message, or NULL (set_without_message).

Copied with git_str_puts into the thread's error buffer during the call; never retained (the header's 'static string' wording is wrong: any string works). NULL is rejected by GIT_ASSERT_ARG: -1 and an 'invalid argument' error in release builds, assert() abort under _DEBUG/GIT_ASSERT_HARD (the coverage build). Returns -1 when the thread state cannot be allocated or the copy runs out of memory (buffer then stuck at git_str__oom, `last` at oom_error), 0 otherwise; unlike git_error_set it never consults errno.

Returns the GIT_BUILD_CPU / GIT_BUILD_COMMIT string literal (cmake-configured in git2_features.h) or NULL for any other key or an unrecorded item; never freed, valid while libgit2.so is loaded. Touches no runtime state, so needs no git_libgit2_init.

Returns a string literal naming the compiled-in backend of the feature, or NULL for an unnamed value, a feature not compiled in, or GIT_FEATURE_HTTP (no backend selection). The GIT_ASSERT_WITH_RETVAL paths (a compiled-in feature whose backend define CMake did not set) are unreachable for any CMake-configured build; in release they would git_error_set (pre-init TLS hazard), in Debug they abort. Never freed; needs no git_libgit2_init.
LIBGIT2_VERSION_PRERELEASE string literal in libgit2.so's rodata ("alpha", "beta", "rcN"), or NULL for a final release. Never freed; needs no initialisation.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_MAJOR; NULL dereferenced.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_MINOR; NULL dereferenced.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_REVISION; NULL dereferenced. Always returns 0; needs no initialisation.
GIT_UNUSED(backend): never read or written, so NULL is accepted on observed behaviour; the header documents it as the allocating backend. Rust policies pass NULL.

git__malloc(len): plain, NON-zeroing storage from git__allocator.gmalloc (stdalloc malloc by default). NULL on OOM via git_error_set_oom. HAZARD: before git_libgit2_init (and after the last shutdown) failalloc makes every request fail, and git_error_set_oom then reads the error TLS slot under an uninitialised/deleted key (0), writing &oom_error into another component's TLS block (ASan: unknown-crash in git_error_set_oom, errors.c:170). Rust strategies pin the runtime with their own git_libgit2_init reference first. len 0 is malloc(0): implementation-defined NULL or a unique pointer. Released by git_odb_backend_data_free or, once returned from a backend read callback, by libgit2's own git__free. Holds one object, a byte buffer, or - filled with a copy and its terminator, as git__strdup does (git__strdup is not exported) - a NUL-terminated string that git_strarray_dispose / git_signature_free / git_buf_dispose may release; Rust OdbDataStrFree::dup, OdbDataStrVec::dup_all and their Clone build strings and char** arrays through it.
GIT_UNUSED(backend): never read or written, so NULL is accepted on observed behaviour.

git__free(data) -> git__allocator.gfree: releases any git__malloc/git__calloc/git__realloc storage (an object, a buffer, or a NUL-terminated string) without reading it; NULL is a no-op. Strings: libgit2 makes its strings with git__strdup/git__strndup/git__substrdup (git__malloc) and releases them with git__free in git_strarray_dispose (each element, then the array), git_signature_free (name, email) and git_buf_dispose (ptr), none of which exports a single-string free, so this is the only exported releaser for one libgit2 string or a char** array of them; Rust OdbDataStrFree / OdbDataStrVec drop through it. Frees through the CURRENT allocator, so storage must not outlive a GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR swap.
memcmp over the whole sizeof(git_oid) (type byte first, then all 32 id bytes); read for the call only. Any byte pattern is accepted; may alias b.
As a; may alias a.
memcpy destination, the whole sizeof(git_oid); must not overlap src.
memcpy source, read for the call only; must not overlap out (memcpy).
memcmp over the whole git_oid, == 0; read for the call only; may alias b.
As a.
Type selects the hex size; unknown type -> GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type', -1, nothing written (sets the thread error, so the runtime must be initialised).
Caller buffer of at least git_oid_hexsize(type) bytes (40/64); exactly that many hex digits written, no NUL. Untouched when the type is unknown.
Caller storage filled in place after the length/type checks (memset then nibbles); partially written when a later character is invalid. Never retained.

Counted run of `len` hex characters, not NUL-terminated; read only after the type and 1 <= len <= hexsize checks, stopping at the first non-hex one. GIT_ASSERT_ARG(str) (abort in _DEBUG builds) rejects NULL.
Caller storage filled in place (memset, type, memcpy of git_oid_size(type) bytes); untouched when the type is unknown.
Exactly git_oid_size(type) bytes are read (20 for SHA1, 32 for SHA256) with no length argument: the caller must supply that many. Not read for an unknown type.
Caller storage filled in place: from_prefix memsets it and sets type and id; on failure it may be left partially written (zeroed + some nibbles). Never retained.
NUL-terminated hex text read for the call only: hexsize chars, stopping at the first non-hex one (NUL included), then str[hexsize] only once all hexsize were hex, so any C string is read in bounds.
Reads the 32 id bytes only (memcmp against a zero array); the type byte is ignored.

Types compared first (returns their difference); then the first len hex digits of id, len capped at GIT_OID_MAX_HEXSIZE so at most 32 bytes are read. Returns 0 on match, 1 or the type difference otherwise (not an ordering).
As oid_a.
NULL is accepted (zero-fills str). Unknown type -> -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type'.

Counted buffer of n bytes: the first min(n, hexsize) are hex digits, the rest (when n > hexsize) zeroed; no NUL added otherwise. With oid NULL all n bytes are zeroed. Untouched when the type is unknown.
Unknown type -> -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type'.
Caller buffer of at least hexsize + 1 bytes (41/65): two digits, '/', the remaining hexsize - 2 digits; no NUL. Untouched when the type is unknown.

Mutated in place (trie grown via resize_trie/push_leaf, min_length raised, `full` set at SHRT_MAX nodes). Dereferenced unconditionally. After a failed resize nodes is NULL and a further add crashes. The failed resize (OOM, GIT_ERROR_NOMEMORY) is the only way into the NULL-nodes state; 'OID set full' leaves the trie intact and every later add fails early.

RETAINED: push_leaf stores &text_oid[i+1] as a leaf tail that later adds read, so the string must outlive the shortener (despite the header's 'owned by the user'). NULL returns min_length without reading. Only the characters walked are validated: a short or non-hex id is stored as a tail whose first char later gives git__fromhex == -1, and push_leaf then writes node->children[-1], corrupting the preceding trie node without any sanitizer report. Callers must pass full 40-char hex ids. Only text_oid[0..40) is ever read (the walk stops at i < GIT_OID_SHA1_HEXSIZE and a leaf at depth d holds &text[d], converted only at d <= 39), so no NUL is needed once 40 hex bytes are present; a stored tail may be the one-past pointer &text[40], never dereferenced.
Frees nodes then the shortener (git__free); NULL is a no-op. Does not touch the borrowed text ids its leaves point at. Safe even after a failed add left nodes NULL.

Fresh git__calloc'd shortener with a 16-node zeroed trie, node_count 1; released by git_oid_shorten_free. NULL on allocation failure, or when min_length does not round-trip through int (GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL: error set in release builds, assert(3) abort in _DEBUG builds).
Reads up to git_oid_size(type) id bytes; an unknown type has size 0, so every string compares equal.

NUL-terminated hex, read two digits per id byte until its NUL or the oid's size; an odd last digit is compared as the high nibble with a zero low nibble. Returns -1 at a non-hex digit it reads, which is indistinguishable from a byte difference of -1; characters past the id's size are never read.
As git_oid_strcmp.
As git_oid_strcmp: 0 when strcmp is 0 (so a prefix, or the empty string, matches), -1 otherwise.
NULL formats as "" (out[0] = NUL). Unknown type: empty string plus the 'unknown type' thread error.
Counted buffer of n bytes: min(n - 1, hexsize) digits then a NUL. NULL or n == 0 returns a static "" without writing. An unknown type writes only out[0] = NUL (nfmt's error is set and ignored).
Returns out itself, NUL-terminated within n, or the static string literal "" (must not be written) when out is NULL or n is 0.

Formatted with nfmt into the thread buffer; an unknown type makes nfmt fail WITHOUT writing, and the stale buffer (uninitialised and unterminated on the thread's first call: ASan heap-buffer-overflow in strlen) is returned anyway, with the 'unknown type' error set.

Per-thread buffer of GIT_OID_MAX_HEXSIZE + 1 bytes under thread_str_key, git__malloc'd on the thread's first call (NULL + OOM error on failure). Owned by libgit2: overwritten by the next git_oid_tostr_s on the same thread (also called internally by checkout/refs/odb code), freed at thread exit or by the shutdown hook. Copy it out before any other libgit2 call.

The caller's git_oidarray, borrowed for the call: its ids buffer is released with git__free, the struct itself is not (the caller holds it inline). Dereferenced unconditionally, so NULL crashes. The fields are left as they were: ids dangles afterwards, so the struct must not be read or disposed again without reinitialising it. Accepts {NULL, 0} and any ids from libgit2's allocator.
Out slot: written only on success with a git_signature_now result owned by the caller.
The repository whose config snapshot supplies user.name / user.email; only used for the call.

Optional out slot: NULL is accepted (GIT_ASSERT_ARG(author_out || committer_out) only refuses both NULL), in which case no author is built. Written only on success with a fresh git_signature_new result owned by the caller (git_signature_free). On error both temporaries are released with git__free, leaking their strings; a NULL author_out leaves the slot untouched.
Optional out slot, as author_out, from the GIT_COMMITTER_* variables.
The repository whose config snapshot supplies user.name / user.email; only used for the call.

Out slot, written only on success with a fresh git__calloc'd copy owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Left untouched when source is NULL (returns 0) or an allocation fails (returns -1, leaking the partial copy and any string already duplicated).

Only read: name and email are git__strdup'd (strdup(NULL) crashes, so a signature whose parse lost a string to OOM cannot be copied), when copied field by field. NULL source returns 0 without writing dest (blame's dup_hunk relies on it).

NULL is a no-op. Frees name and email with git__free (either may be NULL after an allocation failure in git_signature__parse), NULLs them, then frees the struct with git__free. Every public owned signature (new/now/default/default_from_env/from_buffer/dup) is released here; commits, tags, notes, reflog entries and blame hunks call it on the signatures they own. Pool copies (git_signature__pdup) must never reach it.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; the whole NUL-terminated signature line `Name <email> secs zone`, read for the call and never retained.

Out slot, NULLed first: on success a fresh git__calloc'd signature owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Its name or email is NULL when the unchecked extract_trimmed allocation failed, yet 0 is returned. On a parse error (GIT_EINVALID) the struct is freed and out stays NULL.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.

Out slot, set to NULL once the arguments pass their asserts: receives a fresh git__calloc'd signature with trimmed git__substrdup copies of name and email (sign derived from the offset), owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Stays NULL on failure (angle brackets, empty trimmed name/email, OOM); an allocation failure for a string leaks the half-built signature.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
Out slot; as git_signature_new, with the current time and local UTC offset (time(), gmtime_r, mktime).

Caller storage filled in place: sets all three members to the stdalloc malloc/realloc/free forwarders and returns 0. Not exported from libgit2.so (declared in git2/sys/alloc.h without GIT_EXTERN, hidden), so it cannot be bound; git_allocator_global_init applies it to git__allocator.

Read only. NULL elements of src->strings are skipped silently, so the copy's count can be smaller than src->count (with spare calloc'd slots). Declared only in deprecated.h and compiled hidden under GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD: not in libgit2.so's dynamic symbols, so Rust copies go through OdbDataStrVec::dup_all instead (same order: array first, then each string; a failure releases the partial copy).

Caller storage, memset to zero first (not disposed: anything it held leaks), then filled with a git__calloc'd array of git__strdup copies; on a failed strdup the partial copy is disposed and `tgt` re-zeroed. GIT_ASSERT_ARG on NULL.

The caller's struct, borrowed for the call (libgit2 never allocates a git_strarray). NULL returns. Frees strings[0..count) and then `strings` with git__free, then memsets the struct to zero, leaving it reusable. Requires the struct to own its array and strings (the OUTPUT contract of git_strarray.strings); a NULL `strings` with count > 0 derefs NULL. With NULL `strings` and count 0 it still calls git__free(NULL), which reads git__allocator unsynchronised against a concurrent first git_libgit2_init, so the Rust policy skips C for that empty state.

Sole invoker git_trace__write_fmt (src/libgit2/trace.h, via git_trace) passes git_str_cstr of a local git_str it formats the message into and disposes right after the call: borrowed for the call only, never NULL (an allocated string, or the static git_str__initstr / git_str__oom sentinel after a failed vprintf), NUL-terminated, arbitrary bytes (server responses are traced verbatim, so not necessarily UTF-8). git_trace call sites: transports/httpclient.c (DEBUG 'Connecting to remote/proxy', 'Sending ... request'; TRACE 'Received:' and the request dump) in every build, and streams/stransport.c:269 (INFO, an SSLRead error) only under GIT_HTTPS_SECURETRANSPORT, out of the campaign's scope. The level argument is always a named GIT_TRACE_* constant at every call site (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE in practice; never NONE). Called on whichever thread runs the traced libgit2 call, concurrently from several threads; the callback reads no payload (none exists), and git_trace__data is read without a lock.
libc malloc: NON-zeroing; NULL on failure. Called directly by the stdalloc/debugalloc backends of git__allocator and by vendored deps (ntlmclient, reftable's default). Released by free.
reftable_malloc(nelem*elsize) then memset 0: ZEROING; NULL on overflow, zero size or failure. Released by reftable_free.
reftable's free hook or libc free; NULL is a no-op. Releases reftable_malloc-family storage.

reftable's allocator: the hook set by reftable_set_alloc (libgit2 installs git__ wrappers in refdb_reftable.c) or malloc. NON-zeroing; returns NULL for sz == 0 and on failure. Released by reftable_free.
